$comment: A step pointing at a dialog names the card, except where the card is too big to have a popover beside it -- the DDS one nearly fills the window, so driver.js gives up and centres the popover over the Create button. That step names the first field instead. Three parts: everything the case editor can make on its own, then the text content in the DDS editor, then back to join the two with the GUIDs those documents turned out to have. Steps gated on `saved` read the file from disk, so they need Autosaving left on. Steps point at the whole document window and name the key in the text -- highlighting the row itself did not survive contact with the tree. Only the first step changes editor for you; the two crossings in the middle are the player's to make.

steps.title: Pick a mod to build in
steps.description: A case lives inside a mod. Choose one you already have — this walkthrough will add a folder to it and leave the rest of it alone.

steps.title: Make a home for the case
steps.description:
Click New content and name it exactly theftgonewrong.

The name matters — the steps after this read the case file by it, and it is what the manifest will point at.

The folder arrives empty. What goes in it is the next step.

steps.title: Put the case in it
steps.description: Everything the folder holds is a file the manifest lists, the case included. Click Add new file.

steps.title: Make it a murder
steps.description:
Name it theftgonewrong and set the type to MurderMO — what describes how a murder is chosen and staged. Leave Copy From at None: this case is written from scratch.

That writes two files, and opens the case for you: the case itself, and the manifest telling the game to load it.

Leave Autosaving on: the steps ahead check your work by reading the files.

steps.title: Say which killer this fits
steps.description:
Find compatibleWith, expand it, add an entry, and set it to SerialKiller.

A motive on its own is not a murderer. This says the serial killer can carry it.

steps.title: Who does this?
steps.description:
Find murdererTraitModifiers. Add an entry, fill its traitList with the desperate ones — Affliction-Destitute at least, plus the addictions if you like — and set scoreModifier to 15.

This does not pick the murderer. It weights who the game is likely to choose.

steps.title: What they bring
steps.description:
Find weaponsPool and add Guns, plus Blades if you want.

Someone holding up a shop brings a weapon with them. That is what separates this from a killing of opportunity.

steps.title: Where it happens
steps.description:
Set allowWork to true, and leave allowHome, allowPublic and allowStreets at false. They sit together, a little over halfway down.

This one happens behind the counter, so the victim's workplace is the only place it can.

steps.title: Who is behind the counter
steps.description:
Find victimJobModifiers. Add an entry whose jobs hold Shopkeeper and ShopAssistant, with a jobBoost of 20.

Not a rule — a heavy thumb on the scale. The game can still pick someone else.

steps.title: Somewhere worth robbing
steps.description:
Find victimCompanyModifiers. Add an entry and fill companies with the places that keep cash: PawnShop, and any of Chemist, HardwareStore or Supermarket.

Set mininumEmployees to 2 — note the game's spelling — so the shop is not a one-person operation.

steps.title: A stranger, not a colleague
steps.description:
Find sameWorkplaceBoost and set it to -3.

A robbery is done by someone who walked in off the street. The negative score pushes the game away from picking a killer who works there.

steps.title: The thing they leave behind
steps.description:
A case is only solvable if it leaves something to find. This one leaves a crumpled note, which takes two files: one for the object on the floor, and one for the evidence it becomes when you pick it up.

Click Add new file.

steps.title: The evidence
steps.description:
Name it CrumpledPaperStickupEvidence, set the type to EvidencePreset, and with Copy From selected choose CrumpledNameCipher.

Copying means you only fill in what differs from that base — which is why this file ends up four lines long.

steps.title: The object itself
steps.description: Add another file: CrumpledPaperStickupInteractable, type InteractablePreset, Copy From CrumpledPaperNameCypher.

steps.title: Join the two
steps.description:
Find spawnEvidence and set it to CrumpledPaperStickupEvidence.

Picking the object up produces that evidence. The name here is the evidence file's presetName, not its file name.

steps.title: Leave it at the scene
steps.description:
Find callingCardPool, add an entry, and set its item to CrumpledPaperStickupInteractable.

Now every murder with this motive drops the note. That is the thread the player pulls.

steps.title: Now the words on the note
steps.description:
Every case file this mod needs now exists. What none of them can say is what the note actually reads — that lives in the other editor.

Change Editing to DDS Text Content.

steps.title: Make a tree
steps.description:
Click Add new....

A tree is a whole document. Making one also makes the message and block inside it, so you get the full chain in one go.

steps.title: Say what it is and what it says
steps.description:
Type Document — the kind of tree that is a page the player reads.

Name it CrumpledNoteStickup, with Hand everything over! as the English line, the killer's words.

The mod's name goes in front of yours; the GUID is what the game follows.

steps.title: What the note says
steps.description:
Three documents were written, not one: this tree, the message inside it, and the block inside that.

The line went straight into the mod's strings file. The block only holds its ID.

steps.title: Keep the GUID
steps.description:
Click the 📄 beside the GUID in this window's title to copy it.

Two of the case files you just made are going to point at this document, and that GUID is how they do it. Paste it somewhere for a moment.

steps.title: The name the papers give them
steps.description:
Add new... again — this time type Message, named MonkierTheftGoneWrong (the game's spelling of moniker, kept so it matches everything else), and the reference uses The Robbery Reaper for the line.

A message is a rung below a tree. This one is not a document anyone reads — it is where the game gets the killer's nickname.

steps.title: Keep this GUID too
steps.description:
Copy this document's GUID as well, once it opens. The case file will need it.

Click → when you have it.

steps.title: One more thing to name
steps.description:
The evidence file you made is called CrumpledPaperStickupEvidence. That is a file name — not something a player should ever have to read. The name they do see comes from a strings file.

Add new... one last time.

steps.title: The file the name goes in
steps.description:
Set the type to Strings file and choose Evidence/evidence.names.

A strings file is not named the way a tree is — it is picked from the paths the game already reads. This is the one the game looks in for what a piece of evidence is called.

steps.title: Call it a crumpled paper
steps.description:
Click + Add row. For the key, put CrumpledPaperStickupEvidence — the name you gave the evidence file. For the text, put Crumpled Paper — what the player reads.

Click out of the box when you are done — that is what writes it.

steps.title: Back to the case files
steps.description:
Both documents exist and both have a GUID. Three fields over in the case files are waiting for them.

Change Editing back to Cases & ScriptableObjects.

steps.title: Open the evidence
steps.description: Find CrumpledPaperStickupEvidence under EvidencePreset and click it.

steps.title: Point it at the note
steps.description:
Find ddsDocumentID and paste the tree's GUID into it — the first one you copied.

This is what makes the evidence show your text instead of the base game's.

steps.title: Open the object again
steps.description: Back to CrumpledPaperStickupInteractable under InteractablePreset.

steps.title: And what it reads as
steps.description:
Find summaryMessageSource and paste the tree's GUID there too.

The evidence points at the note for the case file; this points at it for the object you are holding.

steps.title: And the case one last time
steps.description: Open theftgonewrong.

steps.title: Give the killer a name
steps.description:
Find monkierDDSMessageList and paste the message GUID into it — the second one you copied, not the tree.

This is where the newspapers get the name they print.

steps.title: That is the case
steps.description:
A motive that picks a desperate killer and a shopkeeper victim, staged at the counter, leaving a note that reads in the player's hands and a name for the papers.

What is left is scoring weights — the Boost and ScoreRange fields, which shift how often the game reaches for this case over any other. They are safe to leave at zero: the case works, it is just picked no more often than the rest.

Two things worth trying next, both in the DDS editor: a block can hold several lines and pick between them, and a tree can be styled — paper, colour, font.
